candidate.runtime: Node 22 in a Linux cloud container, 4 CPUs
candidate.note: The fixes this gate made are on the branch, each with the test that fails without it. The checks ran on the branch head named in each row.

items.title: Each representative role does what its role allows and nothing more, end to end

evidence.test: records: each role reads the Marine’s shared entry as its role allows, and only the Marine reads the private one
personnel: the record opens by role, never by being someone’s supervisor, and not for the platform
consoles: the Unit Manager runs G-8’s configuration, the Vantage Administrator runs the service, and neither the other’s
exports: the Marine takes everything of theirs, an SNCO the unit’s shared work, and nobody else’s private entries or another unit
a goal assigned in a unit shows its contributors, by title and amount, only to those who may open them: not to its unit’s other Marines
a counselor who no longer counsels the Marine reads what they wrote but no longer moves it

items.title: A Unit A user cannot retrieve Unit B personnel or records

evidence.test: a Unit A user cannot retrieve Unit B personnel
a leader in one Unit Instance is not told where else a Marine serves
another Unit Instance: no G-8 role reaches G-1’s records by its id
an organization sees only itself, and a platform role confers nothing inside one

items.title: A Unit A Unit Manager cannot change Unit B

evidence.test: a Unit A Unit Manager cannot change Unit B
one Unit Instance cannot re-key the sign-in of an account that serves in another
organization administrators staff the units without reading records, and cannot hand themselves a role that does

items.title: IDs in a path, query or body cannot be manipulated to cross a boundary

evidence.test: IDs cannot be manipulated to cross boundaries
the database keeps the boundary when code is bypassed
nobody else’s record can be moved into another Unit Instance
scopesFor gives each person exactly what scopeFor gives them

items.title: A Unit A report cannot contain Unit B records, nor sub-units the reader does not read in their own right

evidence.test: a Unit A report cannot contain Unit B records
a unit report reads the units beneath only where the reader reads them in their own right
team workload, and its report and export, read the units beneath only where the reader does, and name Marines only where they open member records
a unit-measured goal reads the units beneath only where its setter does, and its contributors only where their reader does

items.title: A Unit A export cannot contain Unit B data, nor a unit the exporter may not export

evidence.test: a Unit A export cannot contain Unit B data
a unit export holds only the units its exporter reads: it needs View shared records, and a role that does not reach down exports its own unit
a unit report leaves as a file only with the export permission in every unit it reads
the AI command brief totals only the units its reader reads, and needs View shared records as well as Export data

items.title: Nobody raises their own authority, in any tier; roles are granted only below one’s own

evidence.test: escalation: nobody raises themselves, whatever tier they start in
a Unit Manager cannot elevate themselves through any door
a Vantage Administrator never names themselves a Lead Unit Manager, and founds nothing they then run
an administrator finds no side door into records: leading a unit, their own join code, widening a role they hold, removing an owner
a role an import, invitation or join code carries waits for an account its maker opened
approving your own duty takes a role that names it, which someone else grants: nobody gives it to themselves, the Unit Leader included
a first sign-in found by its address takes the account alone: a password, passkey, second factor, link or session someone else set up there ends
evidence.note: An account a Unit Manager opened is proven only once nobody but its person holds a way in.

items.title: Vantage Administrators run the service and read no operational records, except through an approved, read-only, audited access

evidence.test: Vantage support reads nothing in an organization until its owners approve, read-only, until they end it
personnel: the record opens by role, never by being someone’s supervisor, and not for the platform
an ordinary member is refused on every listed route, and nothing changes but the record of the refusals

items.title: File downloads enforce record and unit authorization

evidence.test: file downloads enforce record and unit authorization
a file goes only where it was added, whoever added it and wherever they serve now
attachments: a file is exactly as reachable as the record it hangs on
evidence is exactly as reachable as its training: its owner, the unit’s readers, and nobody else
a file’s content, type, size and name are checked on the server, and a download is only ever a download

items.note: Downloads hold for every role. Open mediums on the way in: a record moved into an instance that withholds attachments brings its files, work intake keeps a file the scanner rejected, and an unscanned attachment carries no mark.

items.title: An import cannot inject records into another Unit Instance or onto another person

evidence.test: an import cannot inject records into another Unit Instance
an import never reaches another person’s import, another Unit Instance, or a backup
a spreadsheet Vantage ID updates only the importer’s own record, and undo puts it back
an archive is taken only by a fresh instance: one account, one Unit Instance and no record of any kind

items.title: Audit events cannot be silently rewritten: the log is append-only and its chain shows any rewrite

evidence.test: audit events cannot be silently rewritten, and an instance reads only its own trail
an entry is never changed or removed, and the log is opened only inside a transaction that closes it
AUD-1: a rewrite the integrity check finds shows on every page that shows the chain, at once
the audit log is append-only from every start, even for a database copied without its triggers
a service archive from a newer build, or with its audit trail changed, removed or stripped, is refused and nothing is imported

items.title: Every privileged route is inventoried, refuses the unauthorized, and writes its audit entry

evidence.test: the inventory covers the routers where server/app.ts mounts them
every audit action listed is catalogued, and every action a route writes itself is listed
without a session every listed route answers 401, and nothing changes
moving a unit under another parent says where it sat before, in the trail

items.title: An EDIPI is masked, kept out of trails and exports it does not belong in, and printed only for its own person and their counselor

evidence.test: the Unit Instance audit trail never shows, matches or exports an EDIPI, whether a card was linked or the feed ran
a personal export names other people by rank and name where their username is their card’s EDIPI
the worksheet is the COUNSELING WORKSHEET: its boxes, each EDIPI from its own person’s profile, the rest left to fill in, its marking, never stored

items.title: Sign-in, step-up, sessions and sign-out hold for every method the instance offers

evidence.test: login rejects bad credentials uniformly, and three consecutive failures lock the account in the database
sudo-gated actions refuse stale sessions
a forged, misdirected, expired or replayed ID token is refused, and nothing is signed in
a forged certificate header without the proxy secret does not sign anyone in
in direct mode a revoked card is refused and a good one accepted
a session ends after 15 idle minutes, 10 for an owner, and a background poll does not keep it alive
a session opened, resolved or confirmed under an older authentication epoch is refused, and a challenge without one is spent (F04, C04)
signing out forgets what was opened on this device, in both storages, and keeps everything else
a first sign-in found by its address takes the account alone: a password, passkey, second factor, link or session someone else set up there ends
where cards sign in too, an account found by its address that carries an EDIPI is taken only by a sign-in asserting that EDIPI

items.note: Which methods an MCEN instance accepts, and what assurance its step-up needs, wait on the sign-in method policy (review C06, C07): under OIDC-only the server still accepts passkeys and password step-up. Kept open as defect c06-passkey-accepted-under-exclusive-modes until the service’s sign-in owner decides. Open mediums in the same area: step-up opened by any sign-in, staff signing in by password alone, reset links outliving a credential change, username enumeration by passkey options, and the break-glass script under exclusive modes.

items.title: Personnel facts change as effective-dated history and are never silently overwritten

evidence.test: the history names every path that changes a personnel fact: the Marine, Vantage support, and a script
a bulk change is previewed, applied all or nothing, audited as one batch and row by row
every membership change is kept as history: who, when and why, with one period per stretch and no re-shuffles
what the personnel feed sets, a leader cannot change either, and the feed’s changes are in the history
the database refuses to change a published version, withdraw one in force, bring back a withdrawn one or publish out of order
a filed report is never changed or deleted, in the database itself
the history is append-only at the database

items.note: Two edge paths still overwrite without a history row: a billet changed to another of the same title, and a feed restore after a re-join (open mediums billet-id-change-no-history, feed-restore-overwrites-rejoin).

items.title: Export and import round trip: every record type comes back as itself, linked, dated and once
items.source: Spec §14 definition of done; Task 13; ADR-0019

evidence.test: §14 round trip: a representative account, exported and imported into a clean Vantage, comes back as it was
a workbook comes in by record type: awards stay awards, courses training, duty is duty and never becomes an Activity
exports: selective, workbook and one category, and a record download keeps the record’s read rule
a duty sheet imports as duty: its type by code, a file never says its review or score, and nothing goes in twice
the personal export carries every dataset the Marine owns and none of their secrets
a personal export gives the Marine where they acted from, never the address of anyone who acted on them

items.note: Approved duty comes back for review (a file never approves duty, by design). Restoring personal records before the unit configuration leaves past duty unscored, and a spreadsheet round trip drops who wrote a counseling or recommendation (open mediums restore-order-leaves-duty-unscored, spreadsheet-drops-author).

items.title: The counseling PDF: its two parties and unit readers draw it, the EDIPI only for its own person, PII marked, every draw audited

evidence.test: counseling: its counselor, its Marine and the unit’s leader draw the NAVMC 2795 worksheet; nobody outside the unit’s chain reaches it
a draft is its counselor’s alone: nobody else reads, counts or hears of it
the worksheet is the COUNSELING WORKSHEET: its boxes, each EDIPI from its own person’s profile, the rest left to fill in, its marking, never stored
the PDF renders the same document the same way, and long words flow onto more pages, never cut

items.title: Report PDF and print: title, unit, period, generated date and filters; headers repeat; drawn, not a screenshot; export gated

evidence.test: every report runs, and is one document with its title, subject, period, filters and handling line
a long table prints over pages with its header again on each, and nothing cut off
every chart in every report draws a column of a table beside it, and prints with its source
a file leaves Vantage only with the authority to take it
the handling line is the enterprise’s, on every page and file
report PDF: the Marine draws their own; another Marine’s needs their records opened in the unit
RPT-6: a 5,000-row PDF lets other work run while it draws, and draws the same pages

items.note: Long filter values overprint the filters box, counseling admin boxes clip a three-line billet, and the analysis PDF cuts long titles with an ellipsis (open mediums report-filters-overflow, counseling-admin-clipping, analysis-pdf-truncates-text).

items.title: Financial error reports: snapshots kept as filed, comparisons and KPIs exact, read only within the unit

evidence.test: the second and third reports compare as worked out by hand, a workbook as a CSV
every count is the number of rows its drill holds, and the groups add up to the figures
a filed report is never changed or deleted, in the database itself
reading needs the unit’s shared records, filing posting its work, and figures by Marine its member records
a series in another Unit Instance, or of another type, with the same identifiers changes nothing
money is parsed to exact cents from text, never through a float
a delimited file longer than the intake reads says it was cut, as a workbook’s sheet does

items.note: Two open mediums: an error-report amount with three or more decimals is rounded through a float (amount-float-rounding, against ADR-0005), and re-coding a report type relabels reports already filed (type-recode-relabels-history, section 18).

items.title: The case diagnoser labels every statement, names each recommendation’s source and authority, and keeps each command’s SOPs to it

evidence.test: it answers in the specification’s order, every statement carries one of the five labels, and every recommendation its source and rank
the provenance ladder is the specification’s six tiers, with the training reference and an unvalidated walkthrough between them
a Unit Manager puts the command’s SOPs on file; nobody else does, and nothing on file is ever edited or removed
a Vantage Administrator puts official guidance on file for every Unit Instance, and only official guidance
the candidate calculation reproduces the reference arithmetic in exact cents, citing every input
the diagnoser classifies all eight of the reference’s numerical examples

items.title: Duty scoring is versioned: a policy change never alters points already earned

evidence.test: the calculator gives the spec’s examples
duty keeps the points of the version in force on its day: March under January’s policy stays 4
a later scoring version never changes a decided or waiting duty, and a duty with no score is approved for none
nobody decides their own duty by reviewing: not its Marine, not an SNCO, not the SNCOIC, not the Unit Leader
approved points apart from the calculated ones take the override permission and a reason, are kept with who and why, and never rescore the duty
only a Unit Manager of the Unit Instance publishes or withdraws, and only for its own duty types
duty: the Marine submits, a reviewer decides, nobody their own, and a later scoring version leaves past duty as it was

items.note: Versioning holds through edit, re-approval, reopening, override, import, the bin and a service archive. Three open mediums sit beside it in the review rules: a reviewer may correct a submitted duty’s points by editing it, or bin it, without the override or rejection path, and a duty’s files can change between a reviewer opening it and deciding it.

items.title: WCAG 2.2 AA: axe finds no serious violation on the pages people use, at phone to desktop widths, in both themes, and keyboard focus is kept

evidence.test: core pages have no serious accessibility violations in light and dark themes
the Unit Manager and Vantage Administrator consoles pass WCAG 2.2 AA at
the dialogs people open most pass WCAG 2.2 AA at
every Tab stop shows where focus is
a dialog gives focus back to what opened it
F1/KB-04: the phone menu is a dialog named Menu that holds focus while open and hands it back when it closes
a Marine pages back through who has looked at their record, on a phone too (AUD-5, AUD-7)

items.note: No PDF is tagged for assistive technology (ADR-0032 lists it as not done); a formal assessment with assistive technology users is the accrediting authority’s.

items.title: Pages and exports stay bounded for a command-sized unit: paged reads, fixed statement counts, an export line

evidence.test: the roster and the team list read the same number of statements for a team or a command of thousands
a page reads a fixed number of statements however many Marines are on it
RPT-6: exports are drawn one at a time, and past the line a reader is asked to try again
the overview reads as many statements for many series as for one
AUD-8, AUD-11: past the limits, the personal export says it was cut and a trail export is refused before a row is read
a whole task list longer than its cap keeps the reader’s own open work, in the table’s order, and says how many there were

items.note: Measured in the container, not on the MCEN host: load at the intended concurrency on the intended hardware is evidence only the host can give. scripts/scale-check.ts gave a worst p95 of 16.3 ms at 1,000 Marines and 50,000 records, timing SQL, not routes. Open mediums: record pages still load and audit a whole list and do not yet say in words that it was cut, Correspondence stops at 300 threads, and unit metrics hold the server for about a second at 50,000 records.

items.title: A fresh database reaches the current schema; old ones upgrade with no row lost, once, audited; a newer one is refused; a failed one rolls back

evidence.test: running the migration twice changes nothing the second time
a newer or malformed schema is refused before base DDL mutates the database
a migration that fails is rolled back, recorded, audited and shown until reviewed
a schema upgrade counts every Unit Instance’s rows before and after; one that loses rows is audited, shown to both consoles and reviewed
a new database says which schema it was created at; each migration after is audited once, and restarts add nothing

items.title: Backup, restore and archive: privileged, checked, audited; the chain verifies; another database, a newer schema or an edited trail is refused

evidence.test: npm run restore is privileged, checked and audited; a database put back by hand is noticed
an instance archive loads into a fresh instance with its own chain, and the log is append-only afterwards
changing VANTAGE_SECRET with the old one as VANTAGE_SECRET_PREVIOUS keeps the chain and every stored secret
a restore across a secret change seals the stored secrets again, so the service needs no previous secret afterwards
an archive sealed under another secret, from before archives said so, is refused before anything is replaced
a settings change refused for its metrics changes nothing else either, so nothing is in force that is neither saved nor in the trail
the database, its write-ahead log and its directory are the service’s alone, whatever the umask

defects.title: Today and Work → Tasks show none of a Marine's open tasks once their units hold 20,000 readable tasks; the cut is silent

evidence.test: a whole task list longer than its cap keeps the reader’s own open work, in the table’s order, and says how many there were

defects.note: Verified independently. A whole record list cut at its cap keeps the reader’s own first and answers X-Vantage-Rows; see record-lists-silent-cut-own-entries for what remains.

defects.title: Activities, Readiness, Training, Awards, Counseling and Goals silently drop a leader's or NCO's own entries; each Activities load is 15 MB and writes 1,000 audit entries
defects.note: Partly closed with today-tasks-silent-cut: the reader’s own entries are kept first and the cut is counted in X-Vantage-Rows. The pages do not yet say so in words, and a whole list is still loaded and its reads audited.

defects.title: Work → Correspondence stops at 300 threads without saying so, hiding the reader's own threads behind the unit's
defects.note: Reported with a probe; not independently verified; left open for a later Task.

defects.title: Unit /metrics loads every shared row of the period and the period before into memory and freezes the whole server for 0.8 to 1.4 s at 50,000 records
defects.note: Reported with a probe; not independently verified; left open for a later Task.

defects.title: The unit JSON export builds every shared record in one synchronous response (31.65 MB at 50,000 activities) outside the export queue
defects.note: Reported with a probe; not independently verified; left open for a later Task.

defects.title: Service archive import accepts an archive from a newer build and silently drops columns and tables it does not know

evidence.test: a service archive from a newer build, or with its audit trail changed, removed or stripped, is refused and nothing is imported

defects.title: Service archive import never verifies the audit trail it brings: an edited trail leaves the host's chain broken for good, and a stripped trail imports as 'intact'

evidence.test: a service archive from a newer build, or with its audit trail changed, removed or stripped, is refused and nothing is imported

defects.title: Archive import's 'fresh instance' guard counts only users and activities; a one-account instance's records, second Unit Instance and audit entries are erased

evidence.test: an archive is taken only by a fresh instance: one account, one Unit Instance and no record of any kind

defects.title: An archive without key_check, sealed under another secret, commits, then fails: answered 400, unaudited, chain broken, and the service will not start again

evidence.test: an archive sealed under another secret, from before archives said so, is refused before anything is replaced

defects.title: A restore across a secret change re-wraps the chain key but not stored secrets: the service starts without VANTAGE_SECRET_PREVIOUS and TOTP sign-in fails

evidence.test: a restore across a secret change seals the stored secrets again, so the service needs no previous secret afterwards

defects.title: The audit log's append-only triggers are created only by migration 021; a restored database without them runs with a mutable audit_log

evidence.test: the audit log is append-only from every start, even for a database copied without its triggers

defects.title: Rotating VANTAGE_SECRET (chain key re-wrap and stored-secret reseal) writes no audit entry

evidence.test: a change of VANTAGE_SECRET is in the trail, once, with what it sealed again

defects.title: PUT /api/platform/runtime changes the running service's settings before it validates them; a 400 leaves them changed, unsaved and unaudited

evidence.test: a settings change refused for its metrics changes nothing else either, so nothing is in force that is neither saved nor in the trail

defects.title: Database copies are world-readable while they are written; the start-over backup is never restricted, and browser backups are staged in shared tmpdir

evidence.test: every copy of the database is its owner’s alone from its first page, the script’s new directory too, and a copy that fails leaves nothing

defects.note: Confirmed and fixed (ADR-0040): backupDatabase makes every copy owner-only before SQLite writes to it and removes a copy it made that fails. The browser download, the server backup, both restore copies and the start-over copy use it; a database SQLite cannot read through is kept by copyFilePrivate, owner-only before its first byte, its write-ahead log too; the script makes a new directory 0700.

defects.title: restore.ts does not refuse a pre-022 backup of another database when the live trail is shorter than the backup's

evidence.test: a backup that names no database is this one’s only when the trail here holds its newest entry, so another database’s is refused and never takes this one’s name

defects.note: Confirmed and fixed (ADR-0040): a backup that names no database is this one’s only when the trail here holds its newest entry with the same hash; otherwise it is refused without --different-database and never takes this database’s name.

defects.title: Signing out one of one's own sessions is not audited

evidence.test: signing out one session from the sessions list is in the trail under its id, and signing out this one there is a sign-out

defects.note: Confirmed and fixed (ADR-0040): another session signed out from the list is session_revoked under its id; this session signed out there is a logout.

defects.title: Under OIDC-only (and CAC-only) mode the server accepts passkey sign-in and password step-up, but the login page offers no passkey and the console hint says provider-only
defects.note: Which sign-in methods an MCEN instance accepts, and what step-up must prove, is the sign-in method policy (review C06, C07). It waits on the service’s sign-in owner; the code follows once it is set. The identity review confirmed it again (c06-exclusive-modes-accept-other-methods).

defects.title: The MCEN production profile starts with negative, fractional or huge session, lockout and size limits

evidence.test: a security setting that is negative, a fraction, written as an exponent or hex, or past its range stops the start and names it, on every profile

defects.note: Confirmed and fixed (ADR-0040): every numeric setting is read by envInt, digits only, a safe integer within its range, on every profile; 0 stays in range where it meant never (VANTAGE_INTAKE_RETAIN_DAYS). The quiet clamps are refusals. Tighter STIG ceilings are left to the ISSM (c08-mcen-weak-postures-not-refused).

defects.title: The MCEN profile starts with CAC revocation off, scanning not required, UDP/TCP syslog, plain SMTP and no enterprise identity
defects.note: Reported with a probe; not independently verified. Plain SMTP to the relay is refused on MCEN since ADR-0040 (c18-mcen-smtp-cleartext). The rest are policy for the ISSM: CAC revocation, required scanning, syslog over TLS, an enterprise identity and STIG ceilings on session settings (an idle limit of 15 minutes at most, for example). Left open until the ISSM sets them.

defects.title: With the production default TRUST_PROXY (one hop) and the port reached directly, a client forges its address and evades the per-address sign-in limit
defects.note: Reported with a probe; not independently verified; left open for a later Task.

defects.title: Off-host audit forwarding drops the oldest records during an outage, loses the queue on restart, and counts unread writes as sent
defects.note: Reported with a probe; not independently verified; left open for a later Task.

defects.title: The live database, its WAL and SHM are created 0644 and its directory 0755; the browser backup copy sits in the shared tmpdir before chmod

evidence.test: the database, its write-ahead log and its directory are the service’s alone, whatever the umask

defects.title: On the MCEN profile, mail including password-reset links is sent in clear text to a relay that offers no STARTTLS

evidence.test: on MCEN a reset link never goes to a mail relay that will not start TLS, and an SMTP_URL that sets its own TLS terms stops the start
an SMTP_URL whose sign-in holds a % that starts no escape stops the start and says how to write it, and a workbook retention of 0 still keeps them

defects.note: Confirmed and fixed (ADR-0040): on MCEN the relay transport requires TLS 1.2 or later with a checked certificate, built from the address and sign-in only; an SMTP_URL that is empty, not smtp: or smtps:, sets its own TLS terms, or holds a % in its sign-in that starts no escape stops the start.

defects.title: Record titles, case references and Marine names stay in localStorage after sign-out and expiry

evidence.test: signing out forgets what was opened on this device, in both storages, and keeps everything else

defects.title: With VANTAGE_SCAN_REQUIRED=true and no scanner, the account roster upload is still accepted and applied
defects.note: Reported with a probe; not independently verified; left open for a later Task.

defects.title: Key rotation silently skips sealed values that neither secret opens and reports nothing
defects.note: Reported with a probe; not independently verified; left open for a later Task.

defects.title: Session cap eviction, idle or absolute expiry and the scheduled prune end sessions with no audit entry, and sign-in entries carry no session correlation

evidence.test: a session the limit pushes out, one that runs out on a request and one the prune finds are each in the trail once, under its id, by the service

defects.note: Confirmed and fixed (ADR-0040): session_evicted for the session limit, session_expired for idle or absolute expiry, found by a request or by the prune, each once, under the session’s id, by the service. Sessions ended together by a change (signing out the others, a password or role change) are in that change’s entry, as before.

defects.title: A synced (backup-eligible, backed-up) passkey is registered with no profile check, and removing it leaves the session it opened signed in
defects.note: Reported with a probe; not independently verified; left open for a later Task.

defects.title: Report CSV export carries no handling line, although docs and the test title say every file does
defects.note: Reported with a probe; not independently verified; left open for a later Task.

defects.title: ASVS self-assessment still carries stale or overstated claims (V16.5.2 Met, V15.2 npm audit, V15.1 no SBOM)
defects.note: Reported with a probe; not independently verified; left open for a later Task.

defects.title: Generated import passphrases use modulo-biased random selection (open CodeQL biased-cryptographic-random alert)
defects.note: Reported with a probe; not independently verified; left open for a later Task.

defects.title: A reviewer without Override duty points changes a submitted duty's points by editing it, then approves: no reason, no review history, the Marine not told
defects.note: Reported with a probe; not independently verified; left open for a later Task.

defects.title: A reviewer bins a Marine's submitted duty instead of rejecting it: no reason, no review history, the Marine not told
defects.note: Reported with a probe; not independently verified; left open for a later Task.

defects.title: A duty's files can be removed or swapped between a reviewer opening it and deciding it; the version guard does not cover them
defects.note: Reported with a probe; not independently verified; left open for a later Task.

defects.title: The console's 'Try it' and the duty's scoring basis show a rounded multiplier, so the arithmetic shown does not give the points (5 × 1.88 shown as 9.38)
defects.note: Reported with a probe; not independently verified; left open for a later Task.

defects.title: Files reach a Unit Instance with attachments withheld by moving the record that holds them
defects.note: Reported with a probe; not independently verified; left open for a later Task.

defects.title: Work intake keeps a workbook the scanner rejected, malware bytes included, for 400 days and carries it in the service archive
defects.note: Reported with a probe; not independently verified; left open for a later Task.

defects.title: An attachment stored without a scan carries no 'not scanned' mark anywhere

evidence.test: a file keeps what the malware scan said of it, clean or kept without a verdict, in the answer, the list, the trail and the personal export
042 gives every file kept before it a scan status of unrecorded, takes only the three statuses, and changes no other value

defects.note: Confirmed and fixed (ADR-0040, migration 042): attachments.scan_status is clean, skipped or unrecorded, in the answer, the lists, the trail detail and the personal export. Both file lists mark a file that is not clean.

defects.title: The saved-message import reads and scans the whole file before deciding whether the caller may place it
defects.note: Reported with a probe; not independently verified; left open for a later Task.

defects.title: Work-intake filenames are stored as sent: C1 control characters reach the source list and the append-only audit trail
defects.note: Reported with a probe; not independently verified; left open for a later Task.

defects.title: A binned training shows no evidence, yet its record ZIP export still carries the files
defects.note: Reported with a probe; not independently verified; left open for a later Task.

defects.title: An error report longer than the intake row cap is filed with only its first rows: silently for CSV, and the filed history and every comparison are then wrong

evidence.test: a delimited file longer than the intake reads says it was cut, as a workbook’s sheet does

defects.note: Reported high; the independent check rated it medium (recoverable: withdraw and file again under a higher cap). A CSV now says it was cut, as a workbook’s sheet does, so the page warns before filing. A filed report still does not record that it was cut.

defects.title: Unit Manager changes refused without step-up on /api/orgs succeed through /api/org

evidence.test: a Unit Manager who has not confirmed it is them names no unit leader and removes no Marine through the unit routes, as the console refuses them; a Unit Leader still needs no confirmation
every unit change a Unit Manager makes on Unit Instance authority asks them to confirm it is them first, and nothing changes until they do
a Unit Leader is not asked to rename the unit they lead, and is asked to end someone’s Unit Instance role or to move their unit under a parent they do not lead

defects.note: Confirmed and fixed (ADR-0040). An /api/org change asks for step-up when it rests on Unit Instance authority: a Unit Instance structure role in the unit, and no full authority there from the chain of command from a place as high. Naming a unit leader asks when it rests on the instance’s Manage units; taking someone out of their last unit asks whenever it ends a Unit Instance role, as the console does. A Unit Leader renaming their own unit is not asked.

defects.title: A first organization sign-in found by address ended every way into the account but a card: whoever put the address on an account that carries their EDIPI still signed in to it with their card

evidence.test: where cards sign in too, an account found by its address that carries an EDIPI is taken only by a sign-in asserting that EDIPI

defects.note: Found by the code review of this gate’s own diff. A card cannot be ended from the server, since its holder carries it. Where the instance takes cards, an account found by address that carries an EDIPI is now taken only by a sign-in asserting the same EDIPI (VANTAGE_OIDC_EDIPI_CLAIM); otherwise the link is refused (oidc_card_bound), audited, and nothing changes.

defects.title: On a Unit Instance trail, the search still matched an EDIPI, or part of one, in the words of entries other than a card link, so which entries came back confirmed a guess

evidence.test: the Unit Instance audit trail never shows, matches or exports an EDIPI, whether a card was linked or the feed ran

defects.note: Found by the code review of this gate’s own diff. The search no longer looks in the words of any entry that carries ten digits in a row; such an entry is still found by its action, people, entity and address. No action Vantage writes into a Unit Instance trail carries one today besides a card link, so this closes the words people type.

defects.title: A restore that moved the backup’s keys to the current VANTAGE_SECRET left no key rotation in the trail, since the next start found nothing left to rotate

evidence.test: a restore across a secret change seals the stored secrets again, so the service needs no previous secret afterwards

defects.note: Found by the code review of this gate’s own diff. The restore record carries what was moved, and the start that audits the restore writes the secret_rotated entry by the administrator who authorized it.

defects.title: A browser backup that failed after the copy was drawn, but before it left, left a full copy of the database in the temporary directory

evidence.test: a browser backup that fails before it leaves takes its copy with it

defects.note: Found by the code review of this gate’s own diff. The copy and its private directory go on any failure before the download begins.

defects.title: A page load sent under a session that had just ended, and answered after a newer sign-in, cleared the new sign-in’s cookie, so the person was signed out at once

evidence.test: a page load sent under an ended session and answered after a newer sign-in leaves that sign-in in place

defects.note: Found by the full browser suite on 080fed6: spec 33’s Unit Auditor test lost a fresh sign-in after a role grant ended the old one (about 2 sign-ins in 600 under load). The clear came from the document handler (8db5f10) and the service worker’s fetch of / (031d286), both older than this branch. A document no longer clears the session cookie. A dead cookie opens nothing; without its own marker it counts as signed out, and with its marker still in the browser it gets the app, whose first request is refused and clears the marker, as before.

defects.title: On a host shared with the public site, the service worker’s install kept whatever / answered as the app’s offline copy, so a browser signed out, or holding an ended session, kept the public page and opened it offline

evidence.test: the service worker keeps only the application as its offline copy, whoever installs it

defects.note: Found by the review of the fix above: once a dead cookie counts as signed out, an install in that window was one more way in. Older than this branch for a browser with no session. The install now keeps / only when it is the application (from / or /login), the rule navigations already followed.

defects.title: Every unit, member, role, invitation, join-code and profile change through /api/org made on Unit Instance authority went through without step-up, not only the unit routes the register named

evidence.test: every unit change a Unit Manager makes on Unit Instance authority asks them to confirm it is them first, and nothing changes until they do
full unit authority from a role below a Unit Manager’s place does not stand in for confirming it is them, since whom they outrank comes from the instance

defects.note: Found by the review of stepup-bypass-via-org-router. Fixed with it (ADR-0040); the route inventory marks these routes stepUp: instance_authority and its test reads the check from the code. The PR review found full unit authority from a role placed below a Unit Instance role passed as the chain’s; it asks now.

defects.title: A Marine’s page sent when they last signed in to every leader who could open it, while the roster and the personnel record give it only to those who manage the Marine

evidence.test: when a Marine last signed in is on their page for them and those who manage them, never for a leader who only reads their records

defects.note: Found reading the statistics code. No page showed it. Fixed (ADR-0040): only the Marine and those who manage them (personnelAccess().manageIn) receive it.

defects.title: A unit’s access log listed what a Marine did to a private entry (created, edited, deleted, restored, moved, its files), so a leader refused the entry learned it existed and when it changed

evidence.test: what a Marine does to a private entry stays out of every unit’s access log, in the Unit Instance trail, and a shared entry’s stays in its unit’s

a private contact, thread, workbook, import or report draft stays out of every unit’s access log as a private record does, and so does a duty’s way back to a private activity, which its unit sees leave

defects.note: Found reading the statistics code. Fixed (ADR-0040): an entry about a private entry is filed under its Unit Instance and no unit, decided as it is written: a record or case, and a workbook, import, contact, thread, message, report draft, revision or saved report kept private. Each end of a move is filed as its own row was. A counseling a leader writes keeps its unit. Entries written before keep their unit, since the trail is sealed.
